sources.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5
sources.notes: Launch post, model id claude-opus-5-5. $4/$20 input/output, cache read $0.20 (0.05x base, called out same as Fable/Mythos's 0.025x pattern), cache write $5 (1.25x, 5-minute), fast mode $8/$40 (Claude API first-party only per pricing docs; launch post phrases this as "available in Claude Code and the Claude Platform"). Pricing table verbatim: "Input and output tokens are $4 and $20 per million, 20% less than Opus 5. Cache reads ... are $0.20 per million tokens, 60% less than Opus 5." Launch table (headline table, read from server-rendered <table> cells, columns Opus 5.5/Fable 5.1/Opus 5/GPT-6 Astra/GPT-5.6 Sol) plus a duplicate/consistent set of exact values recovered from inline SVG chart aria-labels per effort level low/medium/high/xhigh/max on Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode v1.1 (Main), CursorBench 4.0, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench, and WANDR — used for the single headline-table performance doc in this pack; the SVG effort-curve series is NOT digitized/ingested here (owned by a separate chart-digitization pass). Footnote 1 verbatim: "Terminal-Bench 4.0: The standard error is ±2.6 pts for Claude Opus 5.5 and ±1.6–2 pts for the other Claude models. The public leaderboard (5 trials/task, Claude Code harness) reports Claude Opus 5 at 51.8%; our setup reproduces it at 52.3%, within noise. GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol figures are as reported by OpenAI." Footnote 2 (AutomationBench) verbatim: "AutomationBench results were run and reported by Zapier. These runs were performed without fallback models, so safeguard interventions were considered failures—this resulted in a lower score than Claude Opus 5.5 would achieve in practice. Claude Opus 5.5 results come from Zapier's own evaluation during early access. Results for Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and GPT-6 Astra come from Zapier's public leaderboard." Footnote 3 (Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1) verbatim: "The standard error is ±3.5–5 pts per model. The public leaderboard (3 trials/task, Claude Code harness) reports Claude Opus 5 at 30.0%; our setup reproduces it at 29.0%, within noise. The GPT-6 Astra figure is as reported by OpenAI." Header note verbatim: "Unless otherwise noted, all Claude Opus 5.5 results use adaptive thinking at max effort. Terminal-Bench 4.0 results are reported for Claude Opus 5.5 at xhigh effort and GPT-6 Astra at high effort, as reported by OpenAI; these represent each model's highest score. Claude Opus 5.5 was evaluated with its production safeguards enabled. When they intervened, cybersecurity tasks were completed by Claude Opus 4.8, and biology and frontier LLM development tasks were completed by Claude Opus 5." Vendor claim verbatim (Terminal-Bench 4.0 section): "Opus 5.5 at default effort beats Opus 5 at max effort for about a fifth of the cost. It matches GPT-6 Astra at about 40% of the cost." Vendor claim verbatim (FrontierCode section): "At default effort (medium), Opus 5.5 scores 54.6%, higher than all other models, beating GPT-6 Astra's top score (53.3%) for about a fifth of the cost per task." Vendor claim verbatim (CursorBench section): "At default effort (medium), Opus 5.5 scores 52.5%, compared to 51.8% for Fable 5.1 (max) and 46.6% for Opus 5 (max). It beats GPT-5.6 Sol's top score (41.7%) by 11 points for about a third of the cost per task." Customer-quote claim verbatim (BigFinance Bench, NOT a vendor benchmark claim about GPT-6 Astra as the brief's prior summary implied): "Financial firms need outputs that are consistently correct. At its lowest effort setting, Claude Opus 5.5 beat Opus 5 at high effort on our BigFinance Bench with about 60% fewer output tokens. Its answers are shorter and better structured, and its slides come out denser, more in line with industry standards." No 1M-context/128K-max-output or tokenizer claim is stated on this page; those come from the models-overview doc, and no tokenizer claim was found in any fetched source. Same evidence class as the Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra launch captures: six same-model effort curves (Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode v1.1 main set, CursorBench 4.0, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench, WANDR) read as EXACT values from the page's inline chart-module SVG aria-labels ("Model · effort: score% $cost"), not pixel digitization. No misaligned-behavior or other bar-chart figure with numeric labels is present on this page (Alignment section is qualitative prose only, no chart). The full 130-point effort-curve series behind this headline table is ingested separately in performance/anthropic-opus5-5-digitized-2026-09.json.

Verbatim: "Requests that set thinking: {\"type\": \"disabled\"} return a 400 error at every effort level" for Claude Opus 5.5 — this is STRICTER than Opus 5, where thinking can only not be disabled at xhigh/max (verbatim: "On Claude Opus 5, thinking cannot be disabled at xhigh or max effort: requests that set thinking: {\"type\": \"disabled\"} at those levels return a 400 error"). Effort levels low/medium/high/xhigh/max apply to Opus 5.5. Per-message effort (beta) supported on Opus 5.5 via beta header mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01; verbatim: "Claude Opus 5.5 also supports changing effort mid-conversation with a per-message output_config". Forced tool_choice (source: tool-use implement-tool-use doc, same 2026-09-22 fetch session): verbatim table row — "Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Mythos 5.1" under forced tool use support: "any and tool return a 400 error"; "auto or none" still work. Computer use (source: computer-use-tool doc, same fetch session): Opus 5.5 requires computer_toolset_20260801 on the Claude API and Google Cloud (does not accept the older computer_20251124 toolset there); on Amazon Bedrock it still accepts computer_20251124.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
sources.notes: Numbers parsed from the page's public Next.js hydration payload (11 vegaLiteSpec objects in self.__next_f.push chunks), NOT digitized from images — exact values, not chart reads. Six same-model effort x cost x quality curves (AutomationBench 1.0.6, Agents' Last Exam V1, Factual error rate on difficult prompts, FrontierCode 1.1 Main, DeepSWE 1.1, OSWorld 2.0 offline-set partial reward) with x-axis always 'Cost per task' (USD, log scale) and y-axis 'Score' (fraction, 0-1) or a named rate; plus five single-point-per-model adversarial-safety bar charts (coding deception, broken-search non-disclosure, Codex reviewer-bypass attempts, warning circumvention, unauthorized message-board action), four of which state effort fixed at maximum in their captions and one (unauthorized agent interaction) with no stated effort. VENDOR-published, so grade C even where a chart's benchmark name/harness is third-party (AutomationBench, FrontierCode, DeepSWE, OSWorld). Point count cross-checked against the page's rendered aria-label point list for the one chart (AutomationBench) whose SVG was present in the raw fetched HTML (31 vegaLiteSpec points == 38 aria-labels - 7 duplicated first-points, exact match); the other 10 charts were not yet client-rendered in this fetch and have no aria-label list to cross-check, so their evidence rests solely on the hydration payload.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card - OpenAI Deployment Safety Hub
sources.notes: Full system card (change log dated through 2026-09-22). Fetched via headless-browser capture (page is behind a Cloudflare JS challenge; plain curl/WebFetch return 403) and converted to text with html2text. This document is safety/preparedness-focused: production-benchmark safe-completion rates, U18 evaluations, agentic safe-completion, vision safety, jailbreak/prompt-injection robustness, HealthBench (length-adjusted), hallucination reduction, alignment/misaligned-outcome rates, monitorability/CoT-controllability, and Preparedness Framework capability evaluations (biological/chemical, cybersecurity, AI self-improvement) plus safeguard/refusal evaluations. It contains NO general capability benchmark tables (no SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, FrontierCode, GDPval, etc.) -- those live in the separate GPT-6 Astra launch page already captured in performance/openai-gpt-6-astra-launch-2026-09.json. Per the 2026-09-22 change-log entries, this card's Section 11 ('GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna') is an appendix ADDED on 2026-09-22 -- the same day GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna launched -- and explicitly states these models are covered by this card, not a separate one: "we've implemented the same set of safeguards for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna that are detailed in the GPT-5.6 System Card for GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna." Many figures in this card are bar/line charts with no printed axis values in the extracted text; per pack rule 2 ('never invent rates or scores'), only prose-stated or table-printed numbers are recorded as scores, chart-only series are listed in missing[].
